around.headline: Delivery worker found murdered near Bellandur Lake
around.summary: A delivery boy was found murdered near Bellandur Lake in Bengaluru, police said. If you work late-night delivery shifts or have a family member who does, share live location with someone during the ride and avoid isolated lakeside stretches after dark.

around.headline: Zepto delivery rider thrashed in Yelahanka New Town, four arrested
around.summary: A Zepto delivery agent was beaten with a wooden stick by a group in Yelahanka New Town who allegedly abused him for not speaking Hindi; police have registered a case and arrested four people. If you're assaulted on a delivery job, use the platform's in-app SOS and file a police complaint immediately rather than settling it on the street.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: KSRTC bus crashes on Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway, two killed
around.summary: A KSRTC bus crashed on the Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway, killing two (reports point to the driver and conductor) and injuring around 24 passengers. If you're booked on an intercity bus this weekend, use a seatbelt where fitted and avoid the front-most seats where possible.

around.headline: Karnataka forms single Bengaluru Urban Mobility Mission to tackle traffic
around.summary: The state government has brought public and private mobility agencies under one new umbrella body, the Bengaluru Urban Mobility Mission, to coordinate the city's traffic and transport planning. It's a structural fix, not an overnight one — don't expect a change in your daily commute yet.

around.headline: Food-safety crackdown widens from 5-star hotel kitchens to their suppliers
around.summary: After raids found rotten vegetables, expired milk and fungal produce at Bengaluru's star-hotel kitchens, the health department has formed 30 special teams and is now inspecting the supply centres and vendors that stock those kitchens. If you eat out often, it's worth asking a restaurant for its current FSSAI hygiene rating before booking a table this week.

around.headline: 'Operation Mukta': ~1,900 detained in 50-location ID-check drive
around.summary: Bengaluru police have deployed roughly 500 personnel across 50 locations under 'Operation Mukta' to identify undocumented immigrants, detaining close to 1,900 people so far, including at least 15 confirmed Bangladeshi nationals; activist groups have accused police of assaulting some of those detained. If you're stopped for an identity check, carrying a valid photo ID — Aadhaar, voter ID or passport — will save you time.

around.headline: US Senate passes bill threatening 100% tariffs on India over Russian oil
around.summary: The US Senate has passed a Russia-sanctions bill that would impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries, including India, that continue buying Russian oil; it still needs to clear the House and be signed into law. If you run an export-facing business or hold India-linked equities, this is worth tracking — it stacks on tariff moves the US has already made this year over the same issue.

street_smart.title: An acquaintance says they know someone inside a state recruitment board and can get you — or your relative — a government job or exam clearance for a lump-sum 'processing fee', no merit list needed. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru/Karnataka news: two Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) staffers were arrested for a 'job-for-cash' bid (The Times of India). Job-scam topics haven't appeared in the last 3 weeks of briefs; the closest recent topics (fake currency, godman fraud, SIR-OTP scam) work through different mechanisms.
street_smart.situation: A friend-of-a-friend, or the acquaintance's 'contact', claims to be a facilitator or insider at a state recruitment board and offers to guarantee a government job or a passing exam result for a lump-sum cash payment — exactly the kind of arrangement two KPSC staffers were just arrested for running.

choices.text: Pay the full amount in cash upfront, trusting the personal connection since 'these things work quietly all the time'.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. As today's KPSC case shows, these arrangements do get caught — and when they do, the money is gone, the job never materialises, and you have no receipt or contract to point to because the deal itself is illegal. Insiders who can fix paperwork today can be arrested tomorrow, taking your money and your case with them.

choices.text: Negotiate the fee down, then pay once you get a lower number.
choices.feedback: Risky. A smaller bribe is still a bribe — you're still funding fraud with no legal recourse if it falls through, and no negotiation makes an illegal 'guarantee' any safer to rely on.

choices.text: Ask the facilitator to put the guarantee in writing before paying.
choices.feedback: Risky. A written promise to fix a government exam or job isn't enforceable anywhere — it can't be taken to court without admitting you tried to bribe a public official, so a 'contract' here protects no one.

choices.text: Refuse, verify any job or exam result only through the recruitment board's official portal or notification, and report the offer to the Lokayukta or the board's vigilance cell.
choices.feedback: Correct. Government selections are published only through official channels — any 'guaranteed for a fee' claim is a red flag by definition. Reporting the approach protects you legally (paying, even as a 'victim', can make you complicit in bribery) and helps investigators trace the racket, the way the KPSC case came to light.

takeaways: Treat any 'guaranteed government job or result for a fee' claim as fraudulent by default — legitimate selections are only ever published through the official recruitment board portal.
Paying a bribe for a job doesn't just risk losing your money — it can make you legally complicit in corruption, not simply a victim if it goes wrong.
Report tip-offs about job-for-cash rackets to the Karnataka Lokayukta or the recruitment board's own vigilance/grievance cell rather than handling it privately.

quiz.question: Bengaluru police's 'Operation Mukta' ID-check drive across 50 locations has detained roughly how many people so far?
quiz.why: At least 15 of those detained have been confirmed as Bangladeshi nationals; if you're stopped for a check, a valid photo ID like Aadhaar, voter ID or passport clears it quickly.

quiz.question: The KSRTC bus crash that killed its driver and conductor and injured around two dozen passengers happened on which route?
quiz.why: It's a high-speed, access-controlled corridor — seatbelts where fitted, and avoiding front-row seats, measurably improve survival odds in bus rollovers.

quiz.question: A bill just passed by the US Senate threatens what tariff rate on India and other countries over continued purchases of Russian oil?
quiz.why: The bill still needs to clear the House and be signed into law before it takes effect — it would stack on tariffs the US has already imposed this year over the same issue.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age at which an Indian citizen can register to vote?
quiz.why: Voter list updates like the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exist specifically to add newly-eligible 18-year-olds and remove ineligible or duplicate entries.

quiz.question: Bengaluru has no major river flowing through it, unlike Delhi, Mumbai or Kolkata. Which river, over 100 km away, is its main external water source?
quiz.why: Bengaluru sits on a ridge between watersheds and depends on lakes plus water pumped uphill from the Cauvery — which is why supply is so sensitive to rainfall variability upstream.
